chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn Jarir, from Abi Basir, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Complete the prayer in four places: in the Sacred Mosque (Mecca), the Prophet's Mosque, the Kufa Mosque, and the Sanctuary of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: And no one should say, based on this report and the report narrated by Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, that completing the prayer is exclusive to the Sacred Mosque and the Kufa Mosque, so that if a person leaves them, there is no completion for him, because it is not impossible that in these two reports the two places were mentioned specifically out of respect for them. Then, in other reports, he mentioned groups [of places] in which these two mosques are included, while others are also included in them, and this is not far-fetched nor contradictory.

And we have previously presented reports that encompass the generality of places, among which are these two mosques, including the first report from Hammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: In the Sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Sanctuary of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). After that, the hadith of Ziyad al-Qandi that he said: Complete the prayer in the two Sanctuaries and in Kufa, and he did not say: In the Kufa Mosque.

As for what we presented from the reports regarding the mention of the two Sanctuaries in a general sense, they are too numerous to count. And if it is established that completing the prayer is in the Sanctuary of Allah and the Sanctuary of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and this is preferred over the mosque in a general sense, even if they were specified in these two reports, so too is it with the Kufa Mosque, because no one distinguishes between the two places.

key_terms.إِتْمَامُ الصَّلَاةِ: Completing the prayer (praying four rak'ahs instead of two) in specific locations
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَبُّ: Recommended (a category of Islamic legal ruling)
key_terms.حَرَم: Sanctuary or sacred precinct, often referring to Mecca, Medina, or Najaf/Karbala

ai.seo_question: Where should a Muslim complete their four-rak'ah prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the juristic debate regarding the recommendation of *qasr* (shortening) prayers in sacred precincts (*haram*). Shaykh al-Tusi highlights Muhammad ibn al-Hasan’s argument that specific mentions of the Kaaba, Medina, Kufa, and Karbala are for emphasis rather than exclusivity, establishing a general principle that sanctuaries warrant this practice. This reflects the Shia scholarly approach of reconciling apparent contradictions in narrations to derive broader legal applicability.
